comments.concern: SizeAndPosition mixes two different DPI sources: the top-left comes from GetDisplayCoordinates (which uses GetActiveDisplay().Dpi), but the width/height are scaled by FlyoutWindowHelper.GetDpiScale(DisplayArea.GetFromPoint(coordinates)).
comments.detail: On mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups the focused-window monitor DPI and the DPI of the monitor at the computed physical point can differ, so the bar is sized with one scale and anchored/clamped with another - mis-sizing or shifting it off the intended monitor. Multi-monitor/DPI is this module's most frequent visual regression class; the size and position must be derived from a single, consistent monitor DPI.

comments.concern: GetRawCoordinatesFromPosition scales window by dpi to compute right/bottom/center anchors, but the caller passes the DIP width while the window is actually shown at widthDip*dpiScale; if the two DPI values diverge the anchor centering/clamping is wrong.
comments.detail: Right/Bottom/Center anchoring subtracts window.Width*dpi from the screen edge/center. If the physical width the UI resizes to (widthDip*dpiScale from a possibly different display) doesn't match window.Width*activeDisplayDpi used here, the bar overhangs the screen edge or is not truly centered - exactly the 'wider than screen / wrong position on second monitor' failures this area has repeatedly hit.

comments.concern: The division operators and zero/DivideByZero guards on Point/Rect/Size are deleted, dropping code that had documented static-analysis fixes and was intended to be unit-test-guarded.
comments.detail: These operators were the subject of prior bug fixes (duplicated condition in Size division, missing width/height zero guards in Rect operator/, #46958/#46959/#46684) and the module guardrail says the Point/Rect/Size operators are covered by Core.UnitTests. The new test project does not test them at all. Confirm there are truly no remaining consumers and that removing historically-fragile geometry helpers without replacement coverage is intentional.

comments.concern: Common now imports Common.Dotnet.AotCompatibility.props and enables AllowUnsafeBlocks with a comment claiming Dictionary<Language,LanguageInfo> is marshaled across the WinRT ABI - contradicting Common's deliberate no-WinRT/POCO design.
comments.detail: PowerAccent.Common was intentionally kept free of CsWinRT projections (it is on the verifyCommonProps exclusion list) so it doesn't 'signal the wrong intent to future contributors.' Common has no WinRT surface, so nothing here marshals across the WinRT ABI; the justification for AllowUnsafeBlocks appears inaccurate. Verify the unsafe/AOT props are actually required and don't undermine the POCO intent.

comments.concern: RunOnUiThread runs hook callbacks inline when HasThreadAccess, else fire-and-forget TryEnqueue; correctness depends entirely on the low-level keyboard hook being installed on the WinUI dispatcher thread.
comments.detail: The comment relies on injection staying ordered before the hook returns. This holds only because InitHook/SetWindowsHookEx runs on the UI thread (PowerAccent is constructed in the MainWindow ctor). If callbacks ever arrive off-thread, TryEnqueue is asynchronous and the swallowed trigger key-up would propagate before the accent is injected, reintroducing the exact ordering hazard the comment warns about. This load-bearing assumption should be asserted, not just commented.

comments.concern: The overlay window sets AppWindow.Title but there is no visible suppression from the taskbar / Alt-Tab switcher, unlike the WPF original which set ShowInTaskbar=False.
comments.detail: The WPF Selector explicitly used ShowInTaskbar="False". A non-activating SW_SHOWNA overlay that leaks into the taskbar or Alt-Tab switcher would be a user-visible regression. Confirm TransparentWindow (or an AppWindow.IsShownInSwitchers=false / presenter setting) keeps this never-activated overlay out of the switcher and taskbar.

comments.concern: Bar width is computed purely as Characters.Count * 48 DIP with the ListView never measured, hardcoding cell width and assuming single-cell glyphs.
comments.detail: Deriving width from item count avoids the racy DesiredSize but bakes in ItemWidthDip=48 and ignores actual glyph/content width; wider glyphs or future multi-glyph entries could clip. Also DescriptionMinWidthDip is 648 while the comment cites the WPF original's 600px MinWidth - the parity claim and the constant disagree. Verify clipping behavior and reconcile the min-width constant.

comments.concern: The launch path becomes the relative 'WinUI3Apps\\PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe'; correctness depends on the runner's working directory being the install root.
comments.detail: If the process is launched with a working directory other than the PowerToys install root, this relative path won't resolve and Quick Accent silently fails to start. Confirm the runner sets cwd to the install root (as ImageResizer relies on) and that all other consumers of the old flat path (bug-report tool, watchdog, any hardcoded lists) were updated alongside ESRPSigning and the verify-installation script.

comments.concern: The keyboard-service WinRT component OutDir moved to WinUI3Apps; ensure every runtime consumer (PowerAccent.Core, the new Core.UnitTests, and the module interface) still finds the projected DLL.
comments.detail: PowerToys.PowerAccentKeyboardService.dll is a WinRT component projected into managed Core. The new PowerAccent.Core.UnitTests outputs to tests\ and references Core transitively; verify the WinRT dll is copied to the test output so the tests load, and that nothing in the install root still expects the service DLL there.

comments.concern: The Terminate() fallback calls Environment.Exit(0) which skips SaveUsageInfo and mutex release; confirm the normal disable/runner-exit path reliably takes the graceful TryEnqueue branch.
comments.detail: Environment.Exit(0) is only meant for the pre-OnLaunched race, but if disable() commonly arrives while the queue is draining, usage-frequency stats would be silently lost on every disable and the graceful App.Window.Dispose path never runs. Verify the steady-state disable path always hits the enqueued cleanup so stats persistence isn't quietly dropped.

comments.concern: PublishAot=true is enabled for the UI while the dependency chain includes UnicodeInformation, CsWinRT projections, telemetry and JSON handling that may not be fully trim/AOT-safe.
comments.detail: Turning on ILC/AOT surfaces trim warnings across the whole graph; if any dependency uses reflection (e.g. Unicode data lookups, settings serialization) the published app can fail at runtime or produce trim warnings that block the build. Confirm an AOT publish actually succeeds end-to-end (not just that the analyzer flags are set) as PowerDisplay does.

comments.concern: The WPF pre-render offscreen move (computed from virtual-screen metrics) was dropped; verify no first-show flicker on the previously used monitor when summoned on another display.
comments.detail: The old Selector deliberately moved the window to virtual-screen-relative offscreen coordinates before Show() to avoid a flash on the previous monitor. The new flow sizes/positions before Show() while hidden, but AppWindow may briefly present at its prior location on a different monitor. Confirm there is no visible flicker/ghost on multi-monitor rapid re-summon.

comments.concern: Removal of 'using System.Management' is unrelated to the Quick Accent UI migration and touches a shared Settings library.
comments.detail: This module's reviewers consistently push back on stray, unrelated changes in migration PRs ('This change still shows up and seems unrelated!'). If this using is genuinely unused it may belong in a separate cleanup; at minimum call out why a Settings.UI.Library edit is part of a PowerAccent UI-framework migration.

comments.concern: Four new tests exercise GetRawCoordinatesFromCaret, but production (GetDisplayCoordinates) only ever calls GetRawCoordinatesFromPosition, and the caret path is DPI-unaware.
comments.detail: The caret helper doesn't scale window by dpi (unlike the position helper), so if it were ever wired up it would mis-place at high DPI; today it is effectively dead code that the tests lock in. Either wire caret placement through GetDisplayCoordinates or note that this path is intentionally unused so the new coverage isn't mistaken for validated production behavior.
